related_questions.question: Can I still take a COVID hardship withdrawal from my 401k?
related_questions.snippet: Normally, any withdrawals from a 401(k), IRA or another retirement plan have to be approved by the plan sponsor, and they carry a hefty 10% penalty. Any COVID-related withdrawals made in 2020, though, are penalty-free. You will have to pay taxes on those funds, though the income can be spread over three tax years.

related_questions.question: Does my employer have to approve my 401k hardship withdrawal?

text_blocks.snippet: No, your employer doesn't have to approve a 401(k) hardship withdrawal, even if you meet the IRS guidelines. While hardship withdrawals are permitted by the IRS for specific situations, whether they are offered in your employer's 401(k) plan is at their discretion.

list.title: Plan Availability:
list.snippet: Your employer's 401(k) plan document must specifically allow for hardship withdrawals. If the plan doesn't include this provision, you cannot make a hardship withdrawal.

list.title: IRS Guidelines:
list.snippet: Even if the plan allows hardship withdrawals, you still need to meet the IRS guidelines for what constitutes a valid "immediate and heavy financial need".

list.title: Employer Discretion:
list.snippet: Your employer (or plan administrator) ultimately approves or denies the specific withdrawal request. They may require documentation to support your claim of hardship.

list.title: Alternative Options:
list.snippet: Some employers may require you to demonstrate that you've exhausted other options for addressing your financial need before approving a hardship withdrawal.
